body.zh-HK:
> 面試官問：團隊想換一個新的 embedding model。新舊 vector 都是 1,536 維，抽幾個 query 出來，top results 看起來差不多。可不可以把新 vector 直接寫進原本 index，今天就換 query model？
>
> 答啱一半嘅答案：維度一樣，即係儲存格式相容；我會把新文件用新 model embed，舊文件慢慢再補。

維度相同只代表兩組數字都放得入同一個欄位，不代表它們位於同一個語意座標系。**Embedding** 是 model 將一段文字變成一串數字；距離較近的向量通常應該代表較相關的內容。可是「近」的意思由 model、normalisation、chunk 規則與 distance metric 一起定義。用 model A 做的 document vector，配 model B 做的 query vector，或把兩者混在同一個 index，可能仍然返回看似合理的結果，卻令 ranking 悄悄失真。

## 每個 vector 都有來歷

把 embedding 當成地圖座標會容易理解。兩張地圖都用四位數 grid，不等於它們把同一間店放在同一個位置；一張可能以一個城市中心作原點，另一張以另一個城市作原點。dimension 是 grid 長度，不是地圖的原點、比例或地名。實際上，document source version、chunker version、embedding model and revision、normalisation、metric、index build config 和 ingestion time 都是 retrieval record 的一部分。它們要連同 vector 一起可追蹤。

先把問題講成 migration，而非 model swap。保留一個完整的舊 index 作 baseline；由同一份可確認的 source snapshot 建立候選 index；讓同一條 query 分別走舊／新 query-plus-index pair。不要只睇幾條好看的 demo。固定 query set 要包括適用條款、相似但錯的文件、過期版本、無答案、不同 metadata filter 和較長的 domain term。每一行要保存 candidate IDs、filter、model/index receipt、top-k、預期 evidence 和 reviewer decision。

## Cutover 要由證據決定

先看 retrieval coverage：正確或可接受 evidence 有冇留在 k 之內；再看錯誤：過期、錯 scope、或不應出現的 document 有冇入榜。再量 route latency、index build time、storage、backfill duration 和 failure rate。若候選在某個關鍵 slice 退步，不能用整體平均蓋過去；那個 slice 可以繼續走舊 index、轉 human review，或令 migration 停在 shadow read。真正的 cutover 應該只改一個可回退的 index pointer，而不是把兩個向量空間混成日後無法拆解的資料庫。

有時較簡單的答案是不要換。若新 model 沒有在固定 case、成本或延遲上證明一個明確改善，保留舊 receipt 和 index 比「追新 model」更可靠。相反，若 source 或 chunk 規則也變了，就算 embedding model 不變，也要當成新的 candidate collection 做同樣比較。

## 留一條可追問的證據鏈

建立 `embedding-index-migration-lab`：

- `fixtures/source-snapshot.jsonl`：虛構文件、source version、chunk rule 和 metadata。
- `receipts/index-manifest.json`：document count、model revision、dimension、normalisation、metric、index config 和 build time。
- `eval/paired-search-cases.jsonl`：固定 query、expected evidence、filter、舊／新 candidate IDs 和 reviewer disposition。
- `evidence/cutover-decision.md`：coverage、critical-slice regression、成本、rollback pointer 和不切換的條件。
- `tests/no-mixed-space.test.ts`：拒絕把不同 embedding receipt 的 vector 混寫進同一 logical index。

這套 artefact 不證明某個 model 普遍較好；它讓人檢查你有冇把換 model 當成一個可回退、可量度的資料 migration。

## 延伸閱讀

[Similarity 高，點解仍然拎錯文件？](/zh-HK/interview-lab/high-similarity-is-not-relevance)、[RAG Index、Chunk、Rerank 同 Cache：每一層都可以搵錯證據](/zh-HK/articles/retrieval-index-chunk-rerank-and-cache) 和 [Public dataset 都要有 source receipt](/zh-HK/interview-lab/a-public-dataset-needs-a-source-receipt)。

## 範圍說明

這是 AI.DOG 的單題練習。documents、models、index receipts、case、metrics、artefact 和結果全是虛構 synthetic 本地草稿材料；不歸屬任何公司，亦不代表任何公司現時或過去的面試流程、live system 或 production outcome。

body.en:
> Interviewer asks: A team wants to replace the embedding model for a knowledge base. The old and new vectors are both 1,536 dimensions, and a few sampled queries have similar top results. Can it write new vectors into the existing index and switch the query model today?
>
> Half-right answer: The dimensions match, so the storage format is compatible. I would embed new documents with the new model and gradually catch up the old ones.

Matching dimensions only means that two arrays fit in the same column. It does not mean they live in the same semantic coordinate system. An **embedding** is a model’s numeric representation of text; vectors that are nearer should usually represent more related content. But what near means is jointly defined by the model, normalisation, chunking rule, and distance metric. Querying document vectors made by model A with model B, or mixing both in one index, can still return plausible-looking results while quietly distorting ranking.

## Every vector has a provenance

A map-coordinate analogy helps. Two maps can both use a four-digit grid without placing the same shop in the same location; one may use one city centre as its origin and the other a different city. Dimension is the grid length, not the origin, scale, or place names. In practice, document source version, chunker version, embedding model and revision, normalisation, metric, index build configuration, and ingestion time belong to the retrieval record alongside the vector.

Frame the work as a migration, not a model swap. Preserve a complete old index as the baseline. Build a candidate index from the same identifiable source snapshot. Send the same query through the old and new query-plus-index pairs. A few attractive demos are not enough. The fixed query set should include an applicable clause, a similar but wrong document, an old version, a no-answer case, different metadata filters, and a long domain term. Each row should retain candidate IDs, filters, model/index receipts, top-k, expected evidence, and a reviewer decision.

## Let evidence choose the cutover

First inspect retrieval coverage: is the correct or acceptable evidence still inside k? Then inspect the bad results: did a stale, wrong-scope, or forbidden document enter the list? Measure route latency, index build time, storage, backfill duration, and failure rate too. A regression on a critical slice cannot be hidden by an overall average. That slice can remain on the old index, route to human review, or keep the migration in shadow read. A real cutover changes one reversible index pointer; it does not blend two vector spaces into a database that can no longer be explained.

Sometimes the simpler decision is not to switch. If the new model has not shown a stated improvement on fixed cases, cost, or latency, preserving the old receipt and index is more reliable than chasing a newer model. Conversely, changing the source or chunk rule deserves the same candidate-collection comparison even when the embedding model stays unchanged.

## An evidence trail a reviewer can inspect

Build `embedding-index-migration-lab` with:

- `fixtures/source-snapshot.jsonl` containing fictional documents, source versions, chunk rules, and metadata.
- `receipts/index-manifest.json` recording document count, model revision, dimension, normalisation, metric, index configuration, and build time.
- `eval/paired-search-cases.jsonl` containing fixed queries, expected evidence, filters, old/new candidate IDs, and reviewer disposition.
- `evidence/cutover-decision.md` recording coverage, critical-slice regression, cost, rollback pointer, and the condition not to switch.
- `tests/no-mixed-space.test.ts` rejecting writes that mix different embedding receipts in one logical index.

This does not prove one model is generally better. It lets someone inspect whether you treated a model change as a reversible, measurable data migration.

## Further reading

[High similarity is not relevance](/en/interview-lab/high-similarity-is-not-relevance), [RAG index, chunks, reranking, and cache: every layer can find the wrong evidence](/en/articles/retrieval-index-chunk-rerank-and-cache), and [A public dataset needs a source receipt](/en/interview-lab/a-public-dataset-needs-a-source-receipt).

## Scope note

This is an AI.DOG standalone practice prompt. Documents, models, index receipts, cases, metrics, artefacts, and results are fictional synthetic local-draft material. No company is attributed, and this is not evidence of any company’s current or past interview process, a live system, or a production outcome.
